clue.text: Keeps going with old excuse for arresting people without blemish

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: SUS was the informal name of the old British law letting police stop people on suspicion
a stain is a blemish or mark

explanation.surface: Someone stays clean of any blemish by using an outdated excuse for making arrests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. The 'sus' law was a much-criticised British stop-on-suspicion law, repealed in 1981.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain something is to keep it going or maintain it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: See 25
Rice, possibly past its sell-by date, containing source of protein

indicators.note: the outer word holds the next letter

parts.note: stale food is no longer fresh

indicators.note: the first letter is where the word begins

explanation.surface: Some rice may be out of date but still provide a little protein.
explanation.walkthrough: P, the start of 'protein', goes inside STALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a basic food eaten widely; rice is an example in much of the world.

clue.text: Model turned into painting, perhaps, by painter

indicators.note: the turned piece is placed inside the next word

parts.note: painting is an example of art

indicators.note: the word for posing is read backwards

parts.note: to model for a portrait is to sit

explanation.surface: A model is transformed into a picture by the painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned into' reads as one phrase meaning became, but 'turned' reverses the posing word and 'into' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is one kind of artist, so the specific stands for the general.

clue.text: Ineffectual new prime minister, May, baby-changing?

indicators.note: the letters are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new prime minister called May is mocked as feeble, as though changing nappies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby-changing' looks like nappy duty, but 'changing' rearranges PM, MAY and BABY.
explanation.definitionFit: Namby-pamby describes someone weak and feeble, lacking force.

clue.text: Vehicle in which very old frolic

indicators.note: says the next pieces sit inside the vehicle

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

explanation.surface: Elderly passengers enjoy themselves in a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: V and O go inside CART.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to leap about playfully, a direct synonym pairing.

clue.text: Muscles in the 25

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles

explanation.surface: Muscles are found in the wormwood plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cross-reference: 25 is wormwood, the herb that flavours absinthe.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical name for wormwood is Artemisia absinthium, and the liqueur takes its name from it.

clue.text: Poorly rate poet's musical production

indicators.note: badly done, signalling the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Critics give a poor score to a poet's stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly rate' reads as a verb phrase; 'Poorly' is the anagram signal and 's links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera with spoken dialogue, a kind of musical stage work.

clue.text: Study Indian instrument endlessly picked up by large plant

indicators.note: taken in by, so the instrument goes inside the plant

parts.note: a tree is a large plant

indicators.note: lifted, which in a down entry reads the letters upward
the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the sitar is a long-necked Indian lute

explanation.surface: Someone examines an Indian instrument sitting under a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter, 'picked up' reverses (fitting a down entry), and 'by' means taken in by the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study of a subject.

clue.text: Tense emailer confused by true duration

indicators.note: the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A nervous emailer is baffled by how long something actually takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like a description of the emailer but gives T, which joins EMAILER in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Real time is the actual time elapsed while something happens, as opposed to a delayed or simulated clock.

clue.text: Abstemious Jew in East German city, formerly

indicators.note: means earlier or before, so the city is placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: An ascetic Jewish man is found in a city of the old East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' tempts you to the GDR, but Essen was never there; 'formerly' just puts ESSEN before E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period, known for self-denial.

clue.text: Target met by flirtatious cow?

definitions.meaning: the centre of a dartboard or archery target
a flirting cow makes eyes at the male of her herd, so his eye meets hers

explanation.surface: A target is encountered by a coquettish cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as the male animal's eye, which a flirtatious cow would meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullseye is the central ring of a target, the spot archers and darts players aim for.

clue.text: Buy shares in underwear

parts.note: a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone buys stock in an underwear company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest is to put money into stocks or other assets, which buying shares does.

clue.text: Contretemps resulting in reduced incidence of foot problem?

parts.note: an incidence that is reduced is falling; 'reduced' serves the phrase as well as the cut

indicators.note: cut down, so a letter is removed from the ailment

parts.note: gout is a painful joint condition that often strikes the big toe

explanation.surface: A quarrel leads to fewer cases of a foot complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful idea is falling gout; 'reduced' drops the G from GOUT to leave OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a quarrel or disagreement, as is a contretemps.

clue.text: Safely drops content of guts, gripped by normal pains

parts.note: par means the normal or expected level

indicators.note: the next piece holds the inner letters within it

parts.note: aches are pains

indicators.note: the inside letters of the following word, without its ends

explanation.surface: Someone with stomach pains finds what is in their gut being expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' gives the inner letters of 'guts'; golf's par is the normal score.
explanation.definitionFit: Parachutes as a verb means descends by canopy, which lets someone land from the air without harm.

clue.text: Dotty spinster's starting to hit the booze

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: tippled means drank alcohol habitually

explanation.surface: A dotty unmarried woman begins to drink heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' seems to describe the spinster but means covered in dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippled means marked with many small dots, a literal reading of the adjective.

clue.text: A tyrant keeping up success with unremarkable protagonist

indicators.note: holding the next piece inside

parts.note: Nero was a notoriously cruel Roman emperor

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is read upward

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A tyrant clings on to success alongside a dull main character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the success word, as this is a down entry; 'keeping' puts it inside the emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking heroic qualities.

clue.text: Himalayan born to carry stakes

indicators.note: holding the next word within

parts.note: née means born, used for maiden names
pales are pointed fence stakes

explanation.surface: A mountain dweller was born to carry wagers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stakes' suggests bets, but here means fence posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal lies in the Himalayas, so a person or thing from there is Himalayan.

clue.text: Fairy ring's to meddle ineffectually first

indicators.note: puts the meddling word ahead of the ring word

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle about without real effect
a bell rings, and a ring can mean a bell call

explanation.surface: A fairy ring is said to make people interfere uselessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fairy ring' looks like a single phrase, but the definition stops at 'Fairy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker Bell is the fairy companion of Peter Pan in J. M. Barrie's play.

clue.text: War writer turned refuse collector

indicators.note: read the two pieces backwards

parts.note: Nam is short for the Vietnam War
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A war writer rejected the post of collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a binman is a rubbish collector who empties household bins.

clue.text: Daddy admitting a deity to temple

indicators.note: letting in, so the father word wraps the next pieces

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: A father lets a god into a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple.

clue.text: Hawk's to ride bike, reportedly

indicators.note: as heard, so the word is spelt as another that sounds the same

parts.note: to pedal is to ride a bicycle

explanation.surface: A hawk is going to ride a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' is the verb meaning to sell, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To hawk goods is to sell them from place to place, as a street seller does.

clue.text: First mate crosses border

indicators.note: the friend spans across the border word, holding it inside

parts.note: pal and mate both mean friend
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A first mate on a ship crosses a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' reads as a ship's rank; 'First' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means original or earliest, so it can stand for first.

clue.text: Point to popular pet in cube

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the pet goes inside the cube word

parts.note: a die is a numbered cube used in games
a cat is a common pet

explanation.surface: Someone directs attention to a fashionable pet sitting in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The cube is a single die, not dice.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to show or signal it, much as pointing does.

clue.text: Songs by Queen formerly gave false impression

parts.note: lied means told untruths
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A former queen sang songs that misled.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina; 'formerly' because that reign has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those of Schubert, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Watt replaces joule in Jumbo Crossword compiled in prison

indicators.note: put together anew, signalling a rearrangement
one letter takes the place of another in the following words

parts.note: J is the SI symbol for the joule
W is the SI symbol for the watt

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter assembles a giant crossword while locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap J for W in JUMBO CROSSWORD and rearrange all fourteen letters. Wormwood Scrubs is a well-known prison in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wormwood Scrubs is an actual London jail, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Herdsman to doctor end of message

parts.note: radio operators say over to close a transmission

explanation.surface: A herdsman is asked to attend to the close of a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a verb (tamper with) but gives DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A drover drives cattle or sheep to market, so he is a kind of livestock handler.

clue.text: Very old and wise, apprehending timbre

indicators.note: arresting, so holding the other piece inside

parts.note: sage means wise
timbre is the tone or quality of a sound

explanation.surface: An ancient wise person grasps the quality of a voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehending' means arresting, so the wise word holds the sound word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone-age is used informally of anything hopelessly antiquated, from the prehistoric period.
